ai.title: Fix undefined toolName handling in xml-stream-parser
ai.summary: The xml-stream-parser now explicitly guards against undefined toolName values before attempting processor lookup, preventing potential crashes or silent failures during stream processing. If a tool call lacks a valid string toolName, the system triggers an 'unknown_tool_call' analytics event and emits a specific parse_error via onError, halting further processing for that chunk. This change applies to the backend XML stream parsing logic in backend/src/xml-stream-parser.ts.

eli5.text: The backend service that parses incoming tool calls now safely handles cases where a tool call is missing its required name. When a malformed tool call arrives without a valid name, the system records an analytics event, emits a clear parse error, and stops processing that specific chunk instead of crashing or silently failing. This makes stream processing more resilient to malformed input and is live today.

ai.title: Standardize Sonnet 4.5 model name
ai.summary: Model string anthropic/claude-4.5-sonnet standardized to anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5 across agent definitions and shared constants. Aligns with canonical Anthropic naming. Updates .agents/base.ts, implementation-planner, researcher, reviewer, and common/src/old-constants.ts.

eli5.text: The assistant now refers to its model using Anthropic's official naming convention instead of an older format. The system used to call the model 'claude-4.5-sonnet' but now uses 'claude-sonnet-4.5', matching how Anthropic names it. If you were to check the configuration files that define which assistants use this model, you'd see the updated name in all of them. This is a behind-the-scenes adjustment that aligns the system with the correct naming standard, there's no change in what the model can actually do.

These assistants are internal tools used by the team building the platform, so most people reading this site won't run into them directly. Behind the scenes, a small consistency fix was also applied to one of the review helpers so that all internal agents are labeled the same way.

ai.title: Debounce search query in Agent Store
ai.summary: Added local state and a 300ms timeout effect to `store-client.tsx` to decouple immediate input feedback from query state updates. Prevents excessive re-renders and network requests during typing. Scope limited to the web Agent Store client. Input value binds to `localSearchQuery`, syncing to `searchQuery` via debounced effect.

eli5.text: When you type into the search box in the assistant store, the app no longer treats every keystroke as a command to reload results right away. Instead, it waits briefly after you stop typing before running the search and asking the server for updated results, which avoids a flurry of repeated checks as you type. You still see each letter appear in the box immediately, but the list of assistants on the page only refreshes once your input has settled.

eli5.text: Clicking a documentation section now takes you to its own page instead of scrolling down within a single long page. The old behavior, where clicking a subsection link jumped the view to an anchor and relied on a smooth-scroll effect, has been removed; the sidebar now links directly to dedicated subsection pages. You would notice this if you use the internal docs site: navigation lands on clean, separate pages for each section, with prev/next buttons between them, rather than a single page with hash-based scrolling. This is live today for the docs navigation described above.

eli5.text: The row of suggested assistants you see when opening the assistant picker in the web app now shows different defaults. Three older suggestions were swapped out for three newer ones, so the list that used to begin with the basic assistant now includes different recommended assistants instead. You'd notice this the moment you open the assistant selection menu, where the previously highlighted 'planner', 'deep-thinker', and 'rampup-teacher-agent' options are gone and 'base-max', 'find-food', and 'landing-page-generator' take their place. This is already live as of today's deployment.

ai.title: Update xml-stream-parser test expectations

eli5.text: The system that runs the assistant software has updated its error messages to be clearer and more helpful. When you (or the system) encounter a tool that can't be recognized, instead of just saying 'Tool not found: undefined', it now says something like 'Unknown tool undefined for tool call: { "param1": "value1" }'. This affects developers working on or testing the backend code, not regular users interacting with the assistant. If you look at the test files, you'll see the expected error output has been updated to match the new, more descriptive format.

ai.title: git-diff evals capture all changes since evalCommitSha^
ai.summary: Updated `getCodebuffFileStates` in `evals/git-evals/run-git-evals.ts` to use `git diff ${evalCommitSha}^` instead of staging and diffing. This captures uncommitted changes and any commits made during the eval. Scope limited to internal evals.

eli5.text: The internal evaluation system that measures the AI's coding work now records every change made during an evaluation, even if those changes weren't explicitly saved at the moment they were made. Previously, the system only looked at changes that had been deliberately staged, meaning some work might have been missed if it wasn't saved in that specific way. Now, it captures the full picture from the start of the evaluation through its end, ensuring all modifications are included in the assessment. This only affects how the AI's performance is measured internally.

eli5.text: The evaluation system that coaches the coding assistant through test runs now tells that assistant out of the gate: don't ever ask Codebuff to commit your work with git. You wouldn't see this as a button or setting; it's a behind-the-scenes instruction change in how the assistant is guided during internal quality checks, so its effect is quieter test runs that skip the commit step entirely. This is in place as of today for the internal evaluation tooling only.

ai.title: Add output to main prompt debug log
ai.summary: The `mainPrompt` function in `backend/src/main-prompt.ts` now includes the `output` variable in the debug log payload alongside `agentState`. This provides visibility into the generated prompt content during development. No user-facing behavior or API changes.

eli5.text: When the assistant is putting together its main response to you, it now writes a little more detail into its behind-the-scenes troubleshooting log. That extra note includes the exact text it generated, so if a developer needs to figure out why something went wrong, or just confirm it worked right, they can see both what the assistant knew at the time and what it actually produced. This only shows up in the internal logs used for debugging, so nothing about what you see or how fast it runs changes.

ai.title: Load agents from ~/.agents in addition to project root
ai.summary: Agent loading now scans both project root and `~/.agents` for `.ts` files. `getUserAgentsDirectory` added to `agent-utils.ts` to resolve home path. `load-agents.ts` aggregates files from both directories before processing. Affects `npm-app` agent discovery logic.

eli5.text: When you start the assistant, it now looks for your custom agents in two places: your project folder and a dedicated agents folder in your home directory (like ~/agents on Mac/Linux). This lets you keep personal agents separate from project-specific ones while still loading both automatically. If you had agents stored only in your home directory before, they will now appear alongside project agents; if you had none there, you will notice nothing changed.

ai.title: Codebuff 1.0.500 released with model and agent improvements
ai.summary: Version 1.0.500 of the codebuff package now increments from 1.0.499, bundling several user-facing fixes and refinements shipped earlier in the day across the backend, agent definitions, web store, docs, and SDK. The release standardizes the Sonnet 4.5 model name to anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5 in agent definitions and shared constants, switches the docs-researcher and web-researcher agents from google/gemini-2.5-flash to x-ai/grok-4-fast, and guards the XML stream parser against undefined toolName values by emitting unknown_tool_call analytics and a parse_error. The web Agent Store now loads its search query through a 300ms debounce and refreshes its editors-choice agent list, while docs navigation moves to one section per page, and agent loading scans both the project root and ~/.agents for .ts files. Internal tooling gains include retries for prompt streaming and message cost tracking, explicit enforcement of the run_terminal_command process_type enum in the SDK, optional cwd handling in SDK run(), async callback support for handleEvent and handleStreamChunk, and RunOptions.agent widening to accept an AgentDefinition object.
ai.evidence: Modified npm-app/release/package.json: codebuff package version bumped from 1.0.499 to 1.0.500 as a release-bump commit.

eli5.text: This release refreshes the AI models powering several built-in agents and tightens up how the tool handles streaming responses and search, making the experience more stable and responsive. The web researcher and documentation research agents now use a faster, higher-quality AI model called grok-4-fast. Model names have been standardized so that Anthropic's Claude Sonnet 4.5 is consistently labeled across the app. When something goes wrong during a streaming tool call with an unrecognized tool name, the system now logs a clear error instead of silently failing or crashing. Users of the web-based agent store will see a more responsive search and an updated set of recommended (Editor's Choice) agents, including a new landing-page generator. People who keep their custom AI agents in a home folder can now have those automatically discovered alongside project-level agents. Upgrading gives you better search performance, clearer error handling, and a more reliable experience when running autonomous agents on coding tasks.

ai.title: SDK 0.3.4 enforce runterminalcommand processtype
ai.summary: SDK version bumped to 0.3.4. `process_type` in `run_terminal_command` removed `.optional()` from Zod schema, enforcing explicit enum values. Affects `common/src/tools/params/tool/run-terminal-command.ts` and `sdk/package.json`. Defaults to `SYNC` if omitted.

eli5.text: When your assistant runs a terminal command, the system now strictly requires you to specify whether it should run in the foreground (waiting for the result) or the background. If you don't say which, it defaults to foreground. This keeps things tidy and prevents errors from unclear instructions.

ai.title: Backend throws error when agent input is cancelled
ai.summary: Agent execution loop in `backend/src/run-agent-step.ts` now throws an error when `checkLiveUserInput` returns false, replacing the previous silent `break`. This change ensures that cancelled or stale user inputs are explicitly handled via exception rather than exiting the loop without signal. The scope is limited to the backend agent runner logic. A debug log entry is added before throwing, capturing `userId`, `userInputId`, `clientSessionId`, `totalSteps`, `runId`, and `agentState` for observability.

eli5.text: When you cancel or your connection drops while the assistant is working on something for you, the system used to stop quietly without telling anyone. Now it will record the details of what was happening (like who you are and what request was cancelled) and raise an explicit error so it can be properly handled instead of silently ending. You won't see this happen directly, but it means cancelled requests are now tracked and managed rather than disappearing.

ai.title: SDK cwd parameter made optional
ai.summary: The `cwd` parameter in `sdk/src/run.ts` and `sdk/src/run-state.ts` is now optional. File discovery and indexing skip execution if `cwd` is missing. Tool handlers (`read_files`, `write_file`, `run_terminal_command`, `code_search`) throw explicit errors via `requireCwd` if invoked without a defined `cwd`. State initialization falls back to `process.cwd()` for `projectRoot` when `cwd` is undefined.

eli5.text: When you run an assistant task, you used to always have to tell it where your project folder lives; now you can leave that out, and the assistant will just skip automatically looking at your project files and looking at your code, while still using your current folder as a fallback for finding your project if needed. If you then ask the assistant to do something that genuinely needs to know that folder, like reading or writing specific files, running a command, or searching your code, it will stop and give you a clear error telling you to provide the project folder instead of failing silently. This only affects people who build their own tools on top of the assistant, since the change is in the developer kit they plug into.

ai.title: Allow async handleEvent and handleStreamChunk in SDK
ai.summary: The `handleEvent` and `handleStreamChunk` callbacks in `CodebuffClientOptions` now accept async handlers returning `void | Promise<void>`. The `run` function awaits these handlers in `onError` and `onResponseChunk` to support non-blocking I/O or complex processing within the callbacks. This change is scoped to the `@codebuff/sdk` package (version 0.3.5), specifically `sdk/src/run.ts`.

eli5.text: If you build on top of Codebuff's software kit, the two notification hooks you can plug into, one that fires on each event and one that fires on each piece of streamed text, now accept work that might take some time to finish, like saving data to a file or calling another service, without freezing the rest of the flow. Previously those hooks had to finish instantly; now they can pause and do slower work in the background, and the kit will wait for them to complete before continuing when it needs to report an error or deliver another chunk.

ai.summary: sdk/src/run.ts RunOptions.agent type widened to string | AgentDefinition. run() clones agentDefinitions and appends passed object, extracting id for agentId. Bumps @codebuff/sdk to 0.3.6.

eli5.text: The SDK's main entry point for launching an agent now lets you hand over a full agent definition object directly, instead of requiring you to reference one by its identifier string first. If you pass in a definition object, the system clones it, adds it to the known collection of agents, and uses the definition's own identifier for the run. This means SDK consumers can now programmatically define and spin up custom agents inline without pre-registering them. The change is live today in version 0.3.6.

ai.title: Add retries for message cost tracking
ai.summary: New `insertMessageRecordWithRetries` wraps `insertMessageRecord` with up to 3 attempts and linear backoff (1s * attempt). Throws after max retries to ensure cost data integrity. Scope: `backend/src/llm-apis/message-cost-tracker.ts`, `packages/billing/src/auto-topup.ts`. `getUserCostPerCredit` removed; auto-topup hardcodes 1 cent/credit.

eli5.text: Every time an assistant message is processed and costs need to be recorded, the system now tries to save that cost to the billing database up to three times before giving up. If the save ultimately fails, it throws an error so that no cost data is silently lost. This only affects internal billing and credit-consumption tracking behind the scenes; end users will not notice any change to how the assistant works or how their account is billed.

ai.title: Stripe buy-credits route hardcodes centsPerCredit to 1
ai.summary: web/src/app/api/stripe/buy-credits/route.ts drops getUserCostPerCredit import and call, replacing it with literal 1. Removes async lookup, simplifies conversion to convertCreditsToUsdCents(credits, 1). Internal billing surface only, no CLI/Web/Desktop picker impact.

eli5.text: When you buy credits through the internal billing system that powers our web app, the price is now always locked to exactly 1 cent per credit, regardless of any previous account-specific discounts or rates that used to be checked at the moment of purchase. Previously, the system looked up a custom price for each user before calculating the total; now it skips that lookup entirely and uses the fixed 1-cent value. As a result, your purchase total is computed faster, but any special per-user pricing that once lowered your cost is no longer applied during checkout.

ai.title: Enable retries for promptAiSdkStream
ai.summary: Removed `maxRetries` passthrough in `promptAiSdkStream` to rely on default retry behavior. Added optional `maxRetries` parameter to `promptAiSdk` and `promptAiSdkStructured` type definitions. Set `maxRetries: 3` in `getAgentStreamFromTemplate` for agent streams.

eli5.text: The assistant's helper system now keeps trying when something goes sideways behind the scenes, instead of giving up on the first stumble. When that happens, it will make up to three attempts before stopping. You probably won't notice a difference in daily use, but things that were flaky before may now succeed instead of failing outright.
